Yesterday, the US government announced an update to its list of prohibited foreign-manufactured products, adding 'advanced robotic devices.' Today, a spokesperson for the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed that the ban also applies to robot vacuums.

The robot vacuum ban affects popular brands like Roomba and Roborock, but you can still continue using your existing products.

When the Trump administration announced a ban on 'advanced robotic devices' entering the US yesterday, headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't necessarily require legs—and neither does the FCC's robot ban. FCC Director of Media Relations Katie Gorscak confirmed to The Verge that the ban will also cover robot vacuums. Existing Roombas are not affected, and already-approved models can continue to be imported and sold. However, the government claims that future foreign robots pose a national security risk, and even robot vacuum companies have been asked to commit to manufacturing domestically in the US.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices to carry national security risks, and this reasoning also applies to products that most people consider harmless, such as robot vacuums, robotic lawn mowers, and more.

Unless explicitly approved, or manufactured domestically in the US, they cannot be sold in the United States.

This ban hits the robot vacuum market particularly hard, because mainstream brands like Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all Chinese-owned.

If you already own one of these products, you can continue using it for now without any interference. The FCC won't come to your door and confiscate your robot vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban is implemented, the robot vacuum market could see drastic changes in the foreseeable future. If all this sounds familiar, it's because it mirrors the wireless router ban from a few months ago.

Would you continue using your existing robot vacuum? Why? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
